 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This is the second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.300/2024 registered at Police Station - Banda, District- Sagar (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 306 & 376(D) r/w 34 of IPC.
Applicant is in detention since 17.04.2024.
First application was dismissed as withdrawn.

2. As per prosecution story, on 08.03.2024 when complainant had gone to do labour work,
applicant and co-accused took the deceased for attending a programme in their relative's house where they committed rape with her.
Thereafter, on 12.03.2024 the deceased committed suicide by hanging herself.
On the basis of which, the offence was registered against the applicant and co-accused under aforesaid sections.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
He is in custody since 17.04.2024.
It is submitted that prosecution witnesses have not supported the prosecution story.
The mother of deceased has not stated that from which mobile number, the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17253 2 MCRC-15441-2025 deceased called her.
The FSL and DNA report are also negative.
He has suffered incarceration of about one year.

In support of his contention, learned counsel has placed reliance on the decision of Apex Court in Patel Babubhai Manohardas & Ors. vs. State of Gujarat passed in CRA. No.1388/2014 and decision of Coordinate Bench of this Court in Arun Patel vs. State of M.P. passed in MCRC.
No.51920/2020.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for State has submitted that present applicant and co-accused have committed rape with the prosecutrix after taking her from her home and because of said incident, the prosecutrix has committed suicide.
The prosecutrix had also informed her mother on mobile regarding rape committed by the present applicant and co-accused.
The bail application of co- accused Anikesh Ahirwar has been dismissed on merits by this Court vide order dated 2/04/2025 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 14101/2025.
Hence, bail be not granted to the present applicant.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.
Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case as well as seriousness of the offence, I am not inclined to grant bail to the present applicant.
7. Accordingly, present MCRC stands dismissed.
